text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele asked the General Prosecutors Office and State Revenue Service to ascertain if ministers have violated anti-corruption laws and provide conclusions about the activities of each minister. Shkele said that if ministers are found guilty, they must be dismissed.
- The presidents of Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania, Poland and Ukraine hailed the Russia-NATO accord and agreed to work closely together to build a more secure Europe during a meeting in Tallinn.

- Russia's Ambassador to Latvia, Alexandr Udaltsov, met with parliamentary factions to discuss issues concerning the Russian-speaking population in Latvia and differences between the rights of citizens and non-citizens.
- President Guntis Ulmanis today is going to the Hague to take part in activities dedicated to the 50th anniversary of the U.S. sponsored Marshall plan.
- The cabinet agreed to compulsory automobile insurance.

- Finance Minister Roberts Zile said the annual inflation rate in Latvia in 1997 will exceed nine percent because of the planned increase in excise taxes in July, which could boost inflation by one percent.
